hints.content: The arrow points to all values less than $-4$.
And the point at $-4$ is filled in.
So, the inequality represents everything **less than or equal to $-4$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**


[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at negative 4 and continues left. A closed point is plotted at negative 4 where the line begins.

choices.clue:
The graph of $x < -4$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at negative 4 and continues left. An open point is plotted at negative 4 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/889b8a05a19f7dfc62e3846d4362eccbacb58931)

The graph of $x > -4$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at negative 4 and continues right. An open point is plotted at negative 4 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/052d2a0ad7e0ed0ebced52ff22605478f0cdb0e0)

The graph of $x \geq -4$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at negative 4 and continues right. A closed point is plotted at negative 4 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/8a99cd9ea0dfbbb4b23764e84a1f3e7c351244c8)
